name: סכום טור טלסקופי – מכנה ממעלה שלישית בעזרת שברים חלקיים (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Here is one with a cubic denominator:

\[ \sum_{n\geq {{CT:0}}} {{CT:1}} \]

Expand the general term into partial fractions in order to find the sum of the infinite series.

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Split the term into partial fractions, regroup it as two telescoping differences, and take the limit of the partial sum.
Step 1 — Partial fractions
Write \({{CT:1}}=\frac{A}{n}+\frac{B}{n+1}+\frac{C}{n+2}\). Multiplying by each factor of the denominator and substituting its root (\(n=0,-1,-2\)) gives \(A={{CT:2}},\ B={{CT:3}},\ C={{CT:4}}\):

\[ {{CT:1}}={{CT:5}} \]

Step 2 — Two telescoping differences
Since \(C=-(A+B)\), the term splits as

\[ {{CT:2}}\left(\frac1n-\frac1{n+2}\right)+{{CT:3}}\left(\frac1{n+1}-\frac1{n+2}\right). \]

Adding from \(n={{CT:0}}\) to \(n=N\), the first difference leaves its first two and last two fractions and the second leaves its first and last one:

\[ S_N={{CT:2}}\left(\frac1{ {{CT:0}} }+\frac1{ {{CT:6}} }-\frac1{N+1}-\frac1{N+2}\right)+{{CT:3}}\left(\frac1{ {{CT:6}} }-\frac1{N+2}\right) \]

Step 3 — The limit
The fractions with \(N\) tend to 0, so

\[ \sum_{n\geq {{CT:0}}} {{CT:1}}=\frac{ {{CT:2}} }{ {{CT:0}} }+\frac{ {{CT:7}} }{ {{CT:6}} }={{CT:8}} \]

on_true.feedback:
Well done your answer is correct. Here you obtain a partial fraction decomposition:

\[ a_n = {{CT:5}} \]

So that writing the sum out explicitly gives partial sums of the form

\[ \begin{aligned} s_m = \sum_{n={{CT:0}}}^{m} {{CT:5}} &= \left({{CT:9}}+{{CT:10}}-{{CT:11}} \right) + \left({{CT:12}}+{{CT:13}} -{{CT:14}} \right) \\ &\quad + \left({{CT:15}}+{{CT:16}}-{{CT:17}} \right) + \ldots \\ &\quad + \left({{CT:18}}+{{CT:19}}-{{CT:20}} \right) + \left({{CT:21}}+{{CT:22}}-{{CT:23}} \right) \\ &= {{CT:9}}+\frac{ {{CT:7}} }{ {{CT:6}} }+\frac{ {{CT:24}} }{m+1}-\frac{ {{CT:7}} }{m+2} \end{aligned} \]

Taking the limit as \(m \rightarrow \infty\) of this last expression gives the sum of the infinite series

\[ \lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} s_m = {{CT:9}}+\frac{ {{CT:7}} }{ {{CT:6}} } = {{CT:8}}. \]

on_false.feedback:
You got something wrong here. The partial fraction decomposition of a general element gives in this case

\[ a_n = {{CT:5}} \]

So that writing the sum out explicitly gives partial sums of the form

\[ \begin{aligned} s_m = \sum_{n={{CT:0}}}^{m} {{CT:5}} &= \left({{CT:9}}+{{CT:10}}-{{CT:11}} \right) + \left({{CT:12}}+{{CT:13}} -{{CT:14}} \right) \\ &\quad + \left({{CT:15}}+{{CT:16}}-{{CT:17}} \right) + \ldots \\ &\quad + \left({{CT:18}}+{{CT:19}}-{{CT:20}} \right) + \left({{CT:21}}+{{CT:22}}-{{CT:23}} \right) \\ &= {{CT:9}}+\frac{ {{CT:7}} }{ {{CT:6}} }+\frac{ {{CT:24}} }{m+1}-\frac{ {{CT:7}} }{m+2} \end{aligned} \]

Try simplifying this telescopic expression and taking the limit \(m \rightarrow \infty\) in order to obtain the sum of the infinite series.
